I am an old man from Mtwara, and my cashew trees are what feed my family — the harvest in July and August pays for everything. I do not buy fertilizer for the trees; my father never did, and the sandy soil here does not give much back even if you try. What I must spend money on is sulfur powder, because without dusting the flowers the powdery mildew will ruin my crop, and then the whole year is lost. I will do the slashing, pruning, and collecting myself, but at harvest time my sons help and I hire a few neighbors to speed the picking before the rain comes.
